newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MANCHESTER MISERY ENDS WITH ARSENAL OWN GOAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER MISERY ENDS WITH ARSENAL OWN GOAL.

text.p: Manchester United's misery was ended in fortunate fashion on Saturday as a Nigel Winterburn own goal presented them with a 1-0 home win over fellow premier league title challengers Arsenal.

The 63rd minute breakthrough was a scrappy affair. Ryan Giggs, in the starting line-up for the first time in seven games because of injury, threaded the ball through to Nicky Butt on his left. Defender Martin Keown intercepted with a strong back pass which posed problems for Arsenal goalkeeper David Seaman, who managed only to knock the ball back towards Butt.
Seaman forced Butt to go wide but the United midfielder managed to put in a cross which Winterburn, in an attempt to turn it clear, succeeded only in chesting the ball into his own net.

Arsenal almost grabbed a late equaliser when striker Ian Wright was put clear inside the penalty area. But Peter Schmeichel, widely criticised for his recent performances, blocked the shot magnificently.
The lone goal proved sufficient to end United's run of three league defeats and revived their hopes of retaining the title.
It left them in sixth place, six points behind leaders Newcastle who were surprisingly held 1-1 at home by West Ham.
Newcastle looked to be heading for defeat until veteran Peter Beardsley equalised in the 82nd minute with his 200th league goal.
Newcastle suffered a major blow when they lost England striker Les Ferdinand with a depressed cheekbone as he challenged for the ball in the West Ham penalty area just before halftime.
Manager Kevin Keegan said afterwards the strike could be out for a month to six weeks.
Liverpool pose the main threat to Newcastle following their almost clinical 2-0 win at Leeds which left them in second place just two points behind with a match in hand.
Former England centre-half Neil Ruddock, making only his second start of the season, repaid manager Roy Evans's faith in him with a 13th minute goal.
Stig Inge Bjonebye swung in a near-post corner which was flicked on by Robbie Fowler. Leeds marginally cleared the danger only for Ruddock to stab home his first goal of the season.
Liverpool stayed in control and it was no surprise when Steve McManaman raced clear in the last minute and waltzed around keeper Nigel Martin before slipping the ball into the net.
Wimbledon, third at the start of the day, missed their chance to move into second place when they were held 2-2 at home by lowly Coventry and slipped to fourth.
Chelsea, fielding new 4.5 million pounds ($7.5 million) signing Gianfranco Zola, similarly failed to improve on their fifth place when they managed only a 1-1 draw at Blackburn.
The point enabled the north country club to move off the bottom, at least temporarily, above Nottingham Forest who visit Sheffield Wednesday on Monday.
There was an avalanche of goals at Everton where the home side went 5-0 up in the first 35 minutes against Southampton, recent 6-3 conquerers over Manchester United, and went on to win 7-1.
Gary Speed hit a hat-trick and Andrei Kanchelskis scored twice.
Arsenal's first defeat under new manager Arsene Wenger failed to dishearten the Frenchman.
"We played a good game and were a bit unlucky to lose," he said. "It was a crazy goal, and it is a bit frustrating to lose a big game like that."
Wenger said it was disappointing that Arsenal had failed to take advantage of their chances but he was pleased with their performance.
"Sometimes you have to congratulate your team when they lose. And I would like to congratulate them tonight."
Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson was understandably relieved at the end of the losing run and had a special word of praise for left-winger Giggs.
"He was outstanding. His penetration and balance puts opponents under pressure. We've missed him while he has been out with injury."
While admitting it was a scrappy goal that won the match, Ferguson said United were on top afterwards. "We should have buried them," he said.
